title: streaming-chat-signal-patterns-and-adaptive-retry-walkthrough
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Create a clear ergonomic surface for Python SDK users to consume streaming chat completions as an event stream (fine-grained message/metadata events), plus a reference implementation of an adaptive reconnect + retry strategy that preserves ordering and reduces duplicate tokens. Deliver examples, tests, and migration guidance for callers that currently use simple chunking. This ticket focuses on API shape, runtime semantics, and example patterns rather than optimizing kernel/runtime performance.
acceptance_criteria: A documented Python API that exposes streaming chat as discrete typed events (message_chunk, role_change, tool_call, completion_done, error, resume_token).
SDK provides a built-in reconnect-and-resume helper that uses resume tokens to request only missing segments when the stream cuts out, with idempotency safeguards.
Adaptive retry/backoff policy implemented and configurable (max_attempts, base_backoff_ms, jitter, aggressive_resume_threshold).
Comprehensive examples: simple consumer, resumable consumer with checkpointing, and an asyncio-friendly iterator with backpressure hints.
Unit and integration tests covering ordering, duplicate suppression, and resume semantics.
Migration guide doc (FAQ + common pitfalls) and a runnable notebook demonstrating robustness under simulated network faults.
steps: Design API surface and event enum; review with SDK leads and PM.
Implement event parser that converts raw SSE/chunk frames into typed events.
Add resume-token plumbing and server request header for resume hints.
Implement adaptive retry controller and expose configuration knobs.
Write examples (sync/async) and notebook with injected network faults.
Add unit/integration tests and run performance smoke tests on CI.
Write migration guide and docs; gather feedback from Solutions team.
Submit PR, iterate on review feedback, and land in python-sdk-1.9 release.
implementation_notes: Event model: keep events flat and small to allow easy JSON parsing; include sequence_id + optional resume_token on events that represent commit points.
Backpressure: expose an optional 'credit' callback that advanced consumers can use to signal desired prefetch window; default should be unthrottled for simple users.
Resume semantics: server returns resume_token periodically (e.g., every N tokens or on completion). Clients must persist the last seen token before acknowledging a chunk as durable.
Idempotency: resume requests must include a client-generated idempotency_key to allow server-side dedup when re-sending overlapping tokens.
Network flavors: support chunked-transfer (HTTP/1.1), SSE, and a websocket shim; normalize input into same event stream internally.
Ordering guarantees: best-effort ordering enforced by sequence_id; consumers should be tolerant to out-of-order events during resume windows and SDK will attempt to re-order when possible.
Failure modes: define clear error semantics for transient (retryable) vs terminal (no-resume) errors; surface machine-readable error codes in the event payload.
testing_plan: Unit tests for parser: malformed frames, partial UTF-8 sequences, and unexpected event types.
Integration test: run local server that simulates disconnects at different offsets and verify resume yields contiguous token stream without duplication beyond one retry window.
Load test: simulate 100 concurrent streaming clients to validate default retry controller does not overwhelm runtime or create thundering herd on resume.
Chaos test: inject packet drops and reorders to verify consumer examples do not return corrupted messages.
Docs validation: run the example notebook in CI to ensure it completes under test harness.
